# DzDataView

list/grid switchable collection renderer.

- **Family:** Data display
- **Source:** `packages/core/src/components/data/DzDataView.vue` · types `packages/core/src/components/data/DzDataView.types.ts`

## Usage (verbatim story source from `packages/core/stories/data/DzDataView.stories.ts`, story `ListLayout`)

```ts
export const ListLayout: Story = {
  args: { layout: 'list' },
  render: args => ({
    components: { DzDataView },
    setup: () => ({ args, products }),
    template: `
      <DzDataView v-bind="args" :items="products" data-key="id">
        <template #item="{ item }">${rowTemplate}</template>
      </DzDataView>
    `,
  }),
}
```

## Parts, states and tokens

**Parts** — addressable nodes, emitted as `data-part`. Reach one with the selector, or pass
classes by name through the typed `ui` prop; a typo in `ui` is a type error rather than a class
that lands nowhere.

When your `class` and a `ui` entry set the same Tailwind utility, **your `class` wins**: the
merge order is recipe → `ui` → `class`, and `cn()` is tailwind-merge, so the last one through
takes effect. That is what lets you restyle a wrapper someone else built without `!important`.
